scan.summary: This is Cascade Specialty Chemicals' Emergency Action Plan for their Portland facility, describing procedures for fires, chemical releases, medical emergencies, earthquakes, and other emergencies affecting all 42 employees and contractors. The plan covers alarm systems, evacuation routes and assembly points, accounting for personnel, rescue and medical duties, and annual training requirements. It is a required policy document under Oregon OSHA and federal OSHA rules (29 CFR 1910.38).
scan.freshness_note: This plan was last revised February 2021, now over 5 years old as of September 2026. Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131 and 29 CFR 1910.38(a) require the plan to be reviewed annually and kept current. A new revision is overdue and should be prepared immediately.

gaps.title: Plan not current
gaps.description: The plan was last revised in February 2021 and has not been updated for over five years. The document is stale and does not reflect current building conditions, staffing, or procedures.
gaps.fix: Conduct a full review of the plan in January 2026 (or as soon as possible) and revise it to reflect current conditions. Update the evacuation maps, floor warden roster, first-aid responder assignments, and any changes to facility layout or staffing. Document the revision date on the cover page.

gaps.title: No specification of incident coordinator identity or current contact information
gaps.description: The plan refers to 'the incident coordinator' in sections 4 and 5 but does not name who this person is, provide their contact information, or identify a backup. The identity and availability of this critical role is unknown.
gaps.fix: Add a section identifying the incident coordinator by name and title, with phone number or other current contact information. Name a backup incident coordinator in case the primary is unavailable. Update this information whenever the assignment changes.
gaps.locator: section 4, line 'Any person unaccounted for is reported at once to the incident coordinator'; section 5
gaps.quote: Any person unaccounted for is reported at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point

gaps.title: No procedure for accounting for contractors and visitors
gaps.description: The plan applies to contractors and visitors on site but does not describe how they sign in, how they are accounted for during evacuation, or how floor wardens know they are present.
gaps.fix: Add a procedure requiring contractors and visitors to sign in with the receptionist, including name, time arrived, and area of facility. Specify that the receptionist brings the visitor log to the assembly point. Instruct floor wardens that they must account for any contractors or visitors in their area using the visitor log in addition to the daily sign-in sheet.
gaps.locator: section 1 (scope mentions contractors and visitors); section 4 (accounting procedure uses only sign-in sheet and visitor log without explaining how visitor log is populated)
gaps.quote: applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office staff, and to contractors and visitors while on site

gaps.title: No documented evidence of floor warden and first-aid responder training
gaps.description: The plan states that floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually, but provides no documentation of who has received this training, when, or what the training covered.
gaps.fix: Maintain records of floor warden and first-aid responder training, including dates trained, names of attendees, name and qualifications of trainer, topics covered, and sign-in sheets. Retain records for at least three years. Make these records available for inspection.
gaps.locator: section 6, line 'Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually'
gaps.quote: Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually.

gaps.title: Evacuation map and floor warden roster not provided with this document
gaps.description: The plan references Appendix A (evacuation maps) and Appendix B (floor warden and first-aid responder roster) but these appendices are not included in the document provided. These are essential supporting documents.
gaps.fix: Ensure that current evacuation maps for the warehouse, laboratory, and offices are posted at each exit door and in the document package. Ensure that the floor warden and first-aid responder roster showing current names and assignments is posted beside each evacuation map and retained with the plan. Both must be dated and updated whenever building layout or staff assignments change.
gaps.locator: section 3, line 'Exit routes are posted on the evacuation maps at each exit door'; section 3, line 'Employees assigned as floor wardens (one per area, listed on the warden roster posted beside each evacuation map)'; section 6, references to Appendix A and Appendix B
gaps.quote: Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices); Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)

gaps.title: No documented evidence of evacuation drill records
gaps.description: The plan states evacuation drills are held twice a year, but no records of these drills are provided. There is no documentation of when drills were held, how many people participated, any problems identified, or corrective actions taken.
gaps.fix: Maintain records of each evacuation drill, including the date, time, whether announced or unannounced, number of participants, whether all personnel accounted for, time to evacuate, any problems encountered, and any corrective actions taken. Document that drills occur in spring and autumn as required. Retain records for at least three years.
gaps.locator: section 4, line 'Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn'
gaps.quote: Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.

gaps.title: No documented evidence of monthly fire alarm testing
gaps.description: The plan states the alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month but does not provide records of these tests, including whether each test was performed, what results were observed, or any problems identified and corrected.
gaps.fix: Maintain a log or calendar record of monthly fire alarm testing showing the date, time, who performed the test, any discrepancies found, and any corrective actions taken. Retain records for at least three years. A simple checklist or log sheet is sufficient, showing the facility's compliance with the monthly testing requirement.
gaps.citation: Oregon Fire Code (IFC Section 907.5); Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131
gaps.locator: section 2, line 'The alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead'
gaps.quote: The alarm is tested on the first Monday of each month by the facilities lead.

gaps.title: No procedure for communication with off-site drivers
gaps.description: The plan covers all 42 employees including drivers, but does not describe how drivers who are away from the facility will be notified of an emergency or evacuation order, or how they will be accounted for.
gaps.fix: Add a procedure for how drivers will be notified of facility emergencies (radio, phone, dispatch system). Specify that drivers are not required to return to the facility unless instructed by the incident coordinator or emergency services. Specify how drivers will report their status and location. Include the phone number for off-site communication and the name of the person responsible for driver notification.
gaps.locator: section 1, line 'all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office staff'
gaps.quote: all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office staff

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence in reading the document itself and identifying what is present and what is missing. The plan is clearly written and well-structured. High confidence in identifying gaps against Oregon Administrative Rules 437-002-0131 and 29 CFR 1910.38(a), which are stable requirements that have not changed. The most significant finding is that the plan is over five years out of date and does not meet the annual review requirement. Several gaps match exactly with open findings from an earlier review, confirming their validity. I am very sure the appendices (Appendix A and B) are not included in the document provided. I cannot verify whether those appendices actually exist at the facility or how current they are. The fact_key for number_of_shifts is inferred from the reference to 'two per shift' first-aid responders; the actual number of shifts is not explicitly stated. The fire alarm monitoring service provider (Cascade Fire & Safety) is named, but no phone number or contact details are given in the plan itself. I could not verify current Oregon Fire Code Section 907.5 requirements as my knowledge of specific code sections may be incomplete.

CASCADE SPECIALTY CHEMICALS, LLC
EMERGENCY ACTION PLAN
Portland Facility, 4410 NW Front Avenue, Portland, Oregon 97210
Revised February 2021
1. Purpose and scope
This Emergency Action Plan describes what employees of Cascade Specialty Chemicals do when there is
a fire, chemical release, medical emergency, earthquake or other emergency at the Portland facility. It
applies to all 42 employees at the Portland facility, including warehouse, drivers, laboratory and office
staff, and to contractors and visitors while on site. The plan is kept in the front office and in the warehouse
break room, and a copy is available to any employee on request.
2. Alarm system
The building has a monitored fire alarm system with audible horns and strobe lights in the warehouse,
laboratory, loading dock and offices. The alarm is monitored 24 hours a day by Cascade Fire & Safety
under a service contract. Manual pull stations are located at each exit door. The alarm is tested on the first
Monday of each month by the facilities lead. A continuous horn means evacuate. Three short horns
repeated means shelter in place because of an outdoor hazard.
3. Evacuation procedures
When the continuous alarm sounds, all employees stop work, secure nothing that requires more than a
few seconds, and leave by the nearest marked exit. Exit routes are posted on the evacuation maps at each
exit door and in Appendix A. Warehouse staff leave by the east dock doors or the north pedestrian door.
Laboratory staff leave by the laboratory's own exterior door on the south wall. Office staff leave by the
main entrance or the west stairwell. Do not use the freight lift. Do not return for belongings.
The assembly point is the far north end of the visitor parking lot, beside the flagpole, at least 150 feet
from the building. Employees assigned as floor wardens (one per area, listed on the warden roster posted
beside each evacuation map) sweep their area, close doors behind them, and report to the assembly point.
For a chemical release outdoors or a hazard that makes leaving the building unsafe, the shelter-in-place
signal sounds. Employees move to the interior conference room or the laboratory corridor, close doors,
and the facilities lead shuts down the building ventilation from the mechanical room panel.
4. Accounting for employees after evacuation
At the assembly point each floor warden takes a headcount of the people from their area against the daily
sign-in sheet and the visitor log, which the receptionist brings out. Any person unaccounted for is reported
at once to the incident coordinator at the assembly point, who passes the information to the fire
department on arrival. No one re-enters the building until the fire department or the incident coordinator
gives the all-clear. Evacuation drills are held twice a year, in spring and autumn.
5. Rescue and medical duties
Employees do not attempt rescue inside the building. First aid is given at the assembly point by the
trained first-aid responders (two per shift, named on the warden roster), who bring the first-aid kit and the
AED from the front office. An employee exposed to a chemical is taken to the emergency shower and
eyewash at the loading dock if it can be reached safely, or to the assembly point, and the SDS for the
product is brought to the responders. Emergency medical services are called for any injury beyond minor
first aid.
6. Training and review
Every new employee is walked through this plan, the exit routes for their work area and the assembly
point on their first day. Floor wardens and first-aid responders are trained annually. The plan is reviewed
with all employees whenever it is changed and whenever an employee's responsibilities under it change.
The facilities lead reviews the plan every January and updates the evacuation maps whenever the building
layout changes.
Appendix A: Evacuation maps (warehouse, laboratory, offices)
Appendix B: Floor warden and first-aid responder roster (posted beside each evacuation map)
